Controls how far away entities can render from the player. Higher values increase the render distance at the expense of frame rates.
Controls how fast confetti falls. Needs to be a value between 0.01 and 5.0.
Controls how fast leaves fall. Needs to be a value between 0.01 and 5.0.
Controls how fast the bulbs flicker. Needs to be a value between 0.0 and 2.0.
Controls how fast the snow falls. Needs to be a value between 0.01 and 5.0.

Controls how iMouse.xy is updated when input is enabled.
Enabled: iMouse.xy updates only while the left mouse button is held, then keeps the last held position.
Disabled: iMouse.xy continuously follows cursor movement even when no mouse button is held.
Controls how many explosions spawn. Needs to be a value between 0.01 and 5.0.
Controls how many fireflies appear per group. Needs to be a value between 0.1 and 4.0.
Controls how many groups spawn. Needs to be a value between 0.1 and 4.0.
Controls how many leaves appear. Needs to be a value between 0.0 and 2.0.
Controls how many particles spawn per burst. Needs to be a value between 0.01 and 5.0.

Controls how many times the main animation sequence repeats after the intro has finished.
Enter 0 for endless looping. Enter 1 for a single full playthrough, which is basically not looping.
Use 2 or higher for a fixed number of full repeats.
Controls how much the strings sway. Needs to be a value between 0.0 and 2.0.
Controls how often bursts spawn. Needs to be a value between 0.01 and 5.0.

Controls how often the encoder stores full reference frames instead of relying on delta-style compression.
Lower values usually improve decoding speed and seeking, while higher values usually reduce file size.
Enter a whole number greater than 0. Changing the optimization preset can overwrite this value.

Controls how strongly elements snap to grid lines.
Lower values require more precision.
Higher values snap from further away.

Controls how the shader source is interpreted:
Auto: tries Shadertoy and direct variants automatically.
Direct Fragment: compile as normal fragment shader.
Shadertoy: compile as Shadertoy-style mainImage shader only.
Controls the brightness (gamma) of the game.
Controls the level of mobs spawned by the spawner
Controls the maximum number of particles which can be present on screen at any one time.

Controls the number of mipmaps which will be used for block model textures. Higher values provide better rendering of blocks in the distance, but may adversely affect performance with many animated textures.

Controls the order in which the radar categories are rendered. A lower number means being rendered earlier. However, in the newer Minecraft versions dots are always rendered on top of the icons. The order still applies within dot or icon rendering though.
